one_line: Ahom prince-turned-king who led the Tungkhungia restoration and the 1682 recapture of Itakhuli, driving the Mughals from Guwahati.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, athletic and battle-hardened, medium height with a compact, powerful build.
appearance.face: Oval face with sharp cheekbones, wheatish-brown Assamese complexion, straight nose, strong jaw, a faint old scar on the left eyebrow, and a focused, determined default expression with slightly narrowed, shonen-style eyes.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair oiled and pulled tightly into a small top-knot at the back of the crown, sides neatly smoothed; a narrow red patkai-style cloth band tied around the forehead with the knot and short tails at the back.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate late-17th-century Ahom warrior-noble attire: a long-sleeved, hip-length cotton tunic in muted off-white with a subtle handwoven texture, worn over a fitted sleeveless quilted coat (jangia-style) in deep indigo with narrow vertical stitching; a wide red-and-cream striped gamocha-style sash wrapped twice around the waist and knotted at the left hip, its ends hanging; below, a ankle-length, straight-wrapped dhoti in dull mustard-ochre with a thin dark border, pleated in front for ease of movement; simple dark brown leather belt over the sash to secure the scabbard; on the forearms, plain brown leather bracers; on the feet, sturdy brown leather sandals with straps around the ankle; minimal jewellery limited to a single small gold hoop earring in the left ear and a slender black thread necklace just visible at the neck.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved single-edged ahom-style sword (dao) with a plain iron hilt wrapped in dark brown leather, a simple disc pommel, and a wooden scabbard stained dark brown and banded with two brass rings, worn suspended from his belt on the left hip.

ref_desc: Gadadhar Singha appears as a mid-30s, wheatish-brown Assamese warrior with an oval face, small eyebrow scar, black hair in a tight top-knot with a red forehead band, wearing an off-white tunic, deep indigo quilted coat, mustard-ochre dhoti, red sash, brown sandals, and carrying a curved dao in a dark brown scabbard at his left hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character model of Gadadhar Singha (Gadapani) as a historically grounded late-17th-century Ahom warrior-king: a mid-30s Assamese man with an athletic build, wheatish-brown complexion, oval face, sharp cheekbones, a strong jaw, straight nose, slightly narrowed shonen eyes, and a faint old scar over his left eyebrow giving him a determined, focused default expression. His thick black hair is oiled and pulled into a tight small top-knot at the back of the crown, sides neatly smoothed, with a narrow red cloth band tied around his forehead, the knot and short tails visible at the back. He wears a long-sleeved, hip-length off-white cotton tunic with subtle handwoven texture, over which sits a sleeveless, fitted, quilted coat in deep indigo with vertical stitching, ending just below the waist. Around his waist is a wide red-and-cream striped gamocha-style sash wrapped twice and knotted at the left hip with ends hanging, over a simple dark brown leather belt supporting his scabbard. His lower garment is an ankle-length straight-wrapped dhoti in dull mustard-ochre with a thin dark border, pleated in front for movement, and he has plain brown leather bracers on his forearms and sturdy brown leather sandals with ankle straps on his feet. He wears minimal jewellery: a small gold hoop earring in his left ear and a slender black thread necklace barely visible at the neck. His signature weapon is a slightly curved single-edged ahom-style sword (dao) with a plain iron hilt wrapped in dark brown leather and a simple disc pommel, resting in a dark brown wooden scabbard banded with two brass rings and hanging from his left hip. Show him from head to toe with clear views of face, hairstyle, clothing layers, sash, belt, bracers, sandals, and dao, using a palette of off-white, deep indigo, red, mustard ochre, and dark brown.
